hints: Differentiate $y = x^{1/2} + 4x^{-1/2}$ term by term with respect to $x$.
Substitute $x = 1$ into $\frac{dy}{dx}$ to find the gradient of the tangent at $A(1, 5)$.
Use point-slope form $y - 5 = m(x - 1)$ to write the equation of the tangent.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = x^{1/2} + 4x^{-1/2}$ using the power rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} + 4\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)x^{-3/2} = \frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} - 2x^{-3/2}$$

Evaluate the gradient of the tangent at point $A(1, 5)$:
$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1} = \frac{1}{2}(1)^{-1/2} - 2(1)^{-3/2} = \frac{1}{2} - 2 = -\frac{3}{2}$$

Write the equation of the tangent at $(1, 5)$ in point-slope form:
$$y - 5 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 1)$$
$$y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{13}{2} \quad (\text{or } 3x + 2y = 13)$$

hints: Calculate the area under the horizontal line $y = 5$ between $x = 1$ and $x = 16$: $\text{Area} = 5 \times (16 - 1) = 75$.
Evaluate the definite integral and subtract the curve area from the rectangle area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the rectangle under the line $y = 5$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 16$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{line}} = 5 \times (16 - 1) = 5 \times 15 = 75$$

Set up and integrate the area under the curve $y = x^{1/2} + 4x^{-1/2}$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 16$:
$$\int_1^{16} \left(x^{1/2} + 4x^{-1/2}\right) dx = \left[ \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} + \frac{4x^{1/2}}{1/2} \right]_1^{16} = \left[ \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2} + 8x^{1/2} \right]_1^{16}$$

Subtract the area under the curve from the area under the line:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 75 - 66 = 9$$
